spans.quotation: Unless otherwise stated, the topics and information covered in this report apply to our U.S. operations for the year ended December 31, 2024, and do not include our international operations or the operations associated with the acquisition of Encino Acquisition Partners, which closed on August 1, 2025. However, beginning with the 2023 Sustainability Report, we have included Scope 1 emissions metrics that include our Trinidad operations. Trinidad operations represented 1% of our total net proved reserves as of December 31, 2024, and less than 5% of our total production in 2024. We also considered common voluntary reporting frameworks, including the disclosure framework of the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB), and the recommended disclosure elements of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD).

The metrics in this table and elsewhere in this report have been calculated using the best available information at the time of preparation of this report. The data utilized in calculating such metrics is subject to certain reporting rules, regulatory reviews, definitions, calculation methodologies, adjustments, and other factors. As a result, these metrics are subject to change if updated data or other information becomes available. Accordingly, certain metrics in this table and elsewhere in this report with respect to prior years may be revised from previous sustainability reports to reflect updated data and other information. Any updates to the metrics in this table, prior to our next sustainability report, will be set forth in the Data Tear Sheet posted to the Sustainability section of the EOG website. Further, certain total amounts in this table and presented elsewhere in this report may not equal the sum of their components due to rounding.

The metrics contained in this report have been calculated using the best available information at the time of preparation of this report. The data utilized in calculating such metrics is subject to certain reporting rules, regulatory reviews, definitions, calculation methodologies, adjustments, and other factors. These metrics are subject to change if updated data or other information becomes available. Metrics in this report with respect to prior years may be revised from previous sustainability reports to reflect updated data and other information. Total amounts presented in this report may not equal the sum of their components due to rounding. Percent changes presented in this report may reflect rounding. Crude oil equivalent volumes are determined using a ratio of 1.0 barrel of crude oil and condensate or natural gas liquids to 6.0 thousand cubic feet of natural gas.

note: criteria 1, 3, 4 — 3 of 5. F1 trigger test satisfied: all three spans apply across ≥2 canonical concepts — span 1 (p.11) establishes the report-level boundary and framework alignment covering M1, M3, O1, O2, O7, S1, S3, S4 and all other concepts simultaneously; span 2 (p.7) is a cross-cutting data quality and revision policy footnote applied to all metrics in the Data Tear Sheet which includes M1, M3, O1, O2, and O7 data; span 3 (p.84) restates the same cross-cutting policy and adds the bbl-to-Mcf normalisation convention used across GHG intensity, water, and production metrics. Criterion 1 (quantitative grounding) satisfied: span 3 (p.84) states a specific quantitative normalisation convention — 1.0 barrel of crude oil and condensate or natural gas liquids to 6.0 thousand cubic feet of natural gas — applied cross-cutting across production-normalised intensity metrics for GHG (M1), methane (O1), flaring (O2), water, and safety denominators. Criterion 2 (target-bound) not satisfied: no named cross-cutting target with baseline and target year at the report level is disclosed under F1; emissions targets belong to M5. Criterion 3 (methodology disclosed) satisfied: p.11 states the report-level operational boundary (U.S. operations, year ended December 31, 2024) with explicit treatment of the Trinidad Scope 1 carve-in and Encino Acquisition Partners exclusion; two named voluntary frameworks are aligned to (SASB, TCFD) plus AXPC; p.7 and p.84 state a cross-cutting calculation approach — best available information, subject to reporting rules, regulatory reviews, definitions, and calculation methodologies — and a revision policy (prior years may be revised); together these constitute a cross-cutting methodology disclosure spanning all environmental, safety, and social metrics. Criterion 4 (time horizon) satisfied: p.11 explicitly states 'year ended December 31, 2024' as the reporting period for the full report — this is a report-level time horizon statement applying across all concepts. Criterion 5 (progress tracking) not satisfied: the revision policy in spans 2 and 3 describes a process for updating prior-year data but does not itself constitute cross-cutting multi-year methodology tracking across reporting periods. F1 boundary pitfall checks: (a) concept-specific methodology statements in the Definitions section (p.75–76 — EPA GHGRP for M1, IPIECA for M3, OSHA for O7) belong to their respective concepts and were excluded from F1 spans — they do not apply cross-cutting; (b) the assurance statement on p.11 ('third-party verification') and p.83 ('internationally recognized certification body') belongs to F2, not F1 — not included in spans and not used to set assured = true here; assured = false because no named assurer appears in F1 spans linked to the cross-cutting methodology content. uncertainty_discussed = true: span 2 and span 3 both explicitly acknowledge that metrics 'are subject to change' and 'may be revised' due to reporting rules, regulatory reviews, and other factors — this constitutes explicit acknowledgment of estimation uncertainty at the cross-cutting level. Cross-concept notes: span 1 boundary statement (Trinidad Scope 1 carve-in) directly informs M1, O1, and M5 boundary understanding; span 3 normalisation convention (1 bbl = 6 Mcf) is the same denominator used in GHG intensity (M1), methane intensity (O1), flaring intensity (O2), and water intensity formulas on p.74.
